I will keep it simple and stay with the local pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this rotation fits the climate, the water situation, and the way I know how to work. I do not have formal schooling, so I would rather use a familiar system with stable grain sales than chase riskier cash crops. At my age, I want a plan that I can manage steadily, with timing I already understand and without too much complicated field work.

I will treat this as a grain year, not an experiment year. I will use improved wheat seed because it is reliable and easier to manage, and hybrid maize because it usually gives stronger yield. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, one topdressing at jointing, two to three irrigations depending on rain, and a few pesticide sprays only when disease or aphids show up. After wheat harvest, I will quickly prepare the field and sow summer maize, because losing time after wheat cuts maize yield. On maize, I will put most nitrogen in split applications, give phosphorus and potassium as base, irrigate a couple of times if the summer rain is not enough, and control weeds and insects in a practical way. I would use rotary tillage because it is faster and cheaper for me than deep ploughing every time, and it matches a wheat-maize cycle well.
